title: Optimized surgical treatment and trial management of oncological patients in East Saxony (MISSION4Sax)
summary:
The central aim of the pilot study is making the expertise of the National Center for Tumor Diseases Dresden (NCT/UCC) available to cancer patients in eastern Saxony and harmonizing their treatment at a high level. This includes access to the latest surgical techniques and innovative studies.
Cancer patients have less access to innovative oncology trials in underserved rural areas, although their prognosis is improved by participating in clinical trials.
Eastern Saxony, with more than 2 million inhabitants and only one Comprehensive Cancer Center (CCC) in Dresden, is underserved in terms of the availability of innovative surgical-oncological expertise regarding diagnosis and treatment of complex cancers, including their metastases and local recurrences. Such a shortage in rural areas leads to a higher mortality rate of patients compared to direct access to expert centers. Oncological S3 guidelines for effective cancer care exist, but are not implemented into routine care at regional level across the board. In Eastern Saxony, as in the rest of Germany, there is no central registry for detailed clinical data, laboratory data, biomarker information and patient reported outcomes of cancer patients. 

The study is parted into four subprojects with the following core elements:
Subproject 1: Establishing treatment pathways based on current guidelines for the treatment of tumor diseases.
Subproject 2: In a newly established Cooperative Surgical Indication Tumor Board (CoSITuB for short) study participant's cases will be discussed by consulting physicians of the University hospital of Dresden and local medical specialists. Patient's treatments will be discussed as well as the possibility of participation in clinical trials at the National Center for Tumor Diseases Dresden (NCT/UCC).
Subproject 3: The collection of patient data for evaluation and quality control as part of a registry database.
Subproject 4: The improvement and acceleration of cooperation and exchange between physicians of various disciplines in outpatient and inpatient areas through the employment of flying data nurses as links between all parties involved. An exchange and training program will be established as well.
conditions: Complex underlying oncological disease with a visceral tumor entity (primary, metastases, recurrence): Colorectal (C18, C19, C20), pancreas (C25), esophagus (C15), stomach (C16), biliary tract and liver (C22.0/ C22.1, C23, C24), rare tumor entities

interventions.name: Patients with a complex visceral oncological disease (primary, metastases, recurrence: colorectal (C18, C19, C20), pancreas (C25), esophagus (C15), stomach (C16), biliary tract and liver (C22.0/ C22. 1, C23, C24), rare tumor entities); who will be presented in a new Cooperative Surgical Tumor Board

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	Complex oncological disease, i.e. the extent or type of diagnosis or therapy of the oncological disease exceeds the capabilities of the treating medical facility and requires extended external, interdisciplinary consultation or requires the involvement of an expert center (NCT/UCCs) to provide the indicated treatment,  according to the assessment of the on site physicians
•      Visceral tumor entity (primary, metastases, recurrence): colorectal (C18, C19, C20), pancreas (C25), esophagus (C15), stomach (C16), biliary tract and liver (C22.0/C22.1, C23, C24), rare tumor entities 
•      Ability to consent 
•      Ability to read and understand the German language
•      Being a registered patient with one of the five medical pilot partners in East Saxony
Exclusion criteria:
• Minors under the age of 18,
• Patients who cannot read and understand the German language,
• Patients who are unable to give consent,
• pregnancy
